clue.text: Verbally prompt top waiter, showing impatience

indicators.note: said out loud, so the word for prompt is replaced by a word sounding the same

parts.note: to prompt an actor is to give a cue
a jumper is a top, a knitted sweater

explanation.surface: A customer impatiently tries to hurry along the head waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waiter' is not restaurant staff but someone waiting in line. A jumper is the British word for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pushes ahead in a line is a person waiting who lacks patience, so the description fits.

clue.text: Preliminary match level after lead's lost? Uncertainty that is right

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, and here it is lost, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: level means equal
an if is a doubt or uncertainty
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A report on an early-round fixture full of doubt and sporting jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualifier is an early round or game deciding who goes through to the main competition.

clue.text: Call gents with glee after seeing off all outsiders

indicators.note: each word loses its outside letters, first and last, keeping only its inner part

explanation.surface: Someone shouts cheerfully to the men after waving off visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle a book or person is to name or call them something.

clue.text: European on high hill's peak admires river

parts.note: on high means up

indicators.note: the peak of a word is its top, the first letter in a down entry

parts.note: to rate someone is to think highly of them

explanation.surface: A European up a mountain admires the river below.
explanation.definitionFit: The Euphrates is a major river of Western Asia, flowing through Turkey, Syria and Iraq.

clue.text: Cycling organisation gives you bother

indicators.note: cycling here means letters are moved round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: a setup is an arrangement or organisation

explanation.surface: A cycling club causes you trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the last two letters of SETUP to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to trouble or bother them.

clue.text: Move away from former government head of France

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a British prime minister in the 1800s
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: An ex-leader of the French government departs.
explanation.definitionFit: To peel off is to leave a group or formation, as aircraft or cyclists do when splitting away.

clue.text: Rascal from Bordeaux, say, university demoted

indicators.note: in a down entry a demoted letter is moved lower, further down the word

parts.note: rouge is French for red, and Bordeaux is an example of red wine

explanation.surface: A scoundrel from the French wine region is downgraded at his university.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or mischievous person, a rascal.

clue.text: Box housing small animal

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to box someone is to fight and beat them

explanation.surface: A crate holds a little creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is any animal, especially a large four-legged one.

clue.text: Be thrown with crazed fan being shameless

indicators.note: thrown suggests letters tossed around and landing in a new order

explanation.surface: A wild fan is tossed out for unabashed behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazen-faced describes someone bold and without shame or embarrassment.

clue.text: Shirker nags peers to work

indicators.note: set to work, the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A lazy colleague pesters coworkers to do the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger, figuratively, is a team member who contributes nothing and relies on others.

clue.text: Okay about fungus turning up in outbuilding

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a stable is an outbuilding for horses

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up reads a word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a cep is an edible mushroom

explanation.surface: Someone is fine with a mushroom sprouting in the shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Respectable can mean acceptable or decent enough, the same as okay.

clue.text: One in craft course joining current V&A retrospective

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a rotating course of duties
I is the symbol for electric current
the letters V and A taken as printed

explanation.surface: A craft course is linked to an exhibition at the Victoria and Albert Museum, a London museum of art and design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests arts and crafts at the V&A, but it means an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is a pilot, someone flying in an aircraft.

clue.text: Tools back in trailer wrapped in cloths to dry

indicators.note: wrapped in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: towels are cloths for drying

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Garden tools at the rear of a trailer are swaddled in towels.
explanation.definitionFit: Trowels are small hand implements for digging or spreading plaster.

clue.text: Pick and feel big toe regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here every second one

explanation.surface: Choose and touch your big toe now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the pick of a group, the very best.

clue.text: Diverse team won't ask for certain limits

indicators.note: the clue words limit or enclose the answer, which sits within them

explanation.surface: A varied team refuses to request certain restrictions.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a group drawn from different units or specialisms for a mission.

clue.text: That woman put on records and relatives hide

parts.note: she refers to that woman
EPs are extended-play records
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A woman plays records while her family hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb but is the noun, an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepskin is the hide of a sheep with its wool left on.

clue.text: Told grass to frame nobleman

indicators.note: to frame is to surround, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a count is a nobleman

explanation.surface: An informer tells how they set up an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' reads as British slang for an informer, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Recounted means narrated, as in a story told to someone.

clue.text: Wanting to have tea set after smashing sample

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first

parts.note: to be for something is to be in favour of it, wanting it

indicators.note: smashing breaks letters up and rearranges them

explanation.surface: Someone breaks the tea set and wants a sample of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretaste is an early sample or hint of something to come.

clue.text: Appropriate uniform adopted in elevated place for holidaymakers

indicators.note: adopted in means taken inside, so one letter goes within the other piece
in a down entry elevated means raised up, read from the bottom

parts.note: a resort is a holiday destination
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Uniforms are worn in a hilltop holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Appropriate is the verb, to take for oneself; to trouser money is British slang for pocketing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser something is informally to pocket or take it for oneself.

clue.text: Feline turned over, it understood

indicators.note: turned over flips the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: A cat rolls over and seems to grasp it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means implied or understood without being stated.

clue.text: Maybe Leonardo and Donatello produced result after time

indicators.note: after places the anagram behind the T
produced suggests the letters are made into a new form

explanation.surface: Renaissance artists created results over time.
explanation.walkthrough: The names suggest the Renaissance painters, but here they are Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, a cartoon team named after them.
explanation.definitionFit: In the cartoon, the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles bear the names of four Italian artists.

clue.text: Monster having operation for eye primarily in phases

indicators.note: one thing for another means it replaces it

parts.note: cycles are recurring phases

indicators.note: primarily means taking the first letter

explanation.surface: A monster has eye surgery done in stages.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclops is the one-eyed giant of Greek myth, met by Odysseus.

clue.text: Delivery firm subject to company takeovers

indicators.note: in a down entry being subject to something means lying beneath it

parts.note: UPS is the United Parcel Service, a delivery company

explanation.surface: A parcel company faces corporate buyouts.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a sudden seizure of power, a takeover of government.

clue.text: Flier from women's group found in southern newspaper

indicators.note: found in means the piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
the WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation

explanation.surface: A pilot from a women's club features in a southern paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The swift is a fast bird that spends almost its whole life on the wing.

clue.text: Alarm from a rook trapped in cask

parts.note: per means a, as in once a day

indicators.note: trapped in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a tub is a cask or barrel
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A bird stuck in a barrel causes alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: To perturb someone is to disturb or worry them, to alarm them.

clue.text: Joint is one held by musician

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the lower leg joint of a cooked chicken
second meaning: a stick a drummer holds to play

explanation.walkthrough: The joint is a cut of poultry, not a body part or a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the cooked leg of a fowl and the stick a percussionist beats with.

clue.text: Drink that's less fizzy uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer covering of letters at each end is removed

parts.note: flatter means less fizzy

explanation.surface: A drink that has lost its sparkle is left exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is a coffee drink made with espresso and steamed milk.

clue.text: Studied industries changing over century

indicators.note: changing over suggests the letters switch round into a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for century, a hundred

explanation.surface: A historian examined how industry altered across a hundred years.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutinised means examined closely and critically.
